'''Claudio Maccone''' (6 February 1948 – 20 August 2025) was an Italian [[SETI]] astronomer, space scientist and mathematician.<ref name=SETIaward>{{cite web|url=http://www.setileague.org/press/pres0205.htm|title=SETI League Awards Highest Honors (Press release)|publisher=The SETI League, Inc.|date=27 April 2002}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Maccone was born on 6 February 1948.<ref name=Bio>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maccone.com/|title=Dr. Claudio Maccone, Ph. D.|website=www.maccone.com}}</ref> He obtained two degrees from the [[University of Turin]]: in physics in 1972 and in mathematics in 1974.{{Citation needed|date=July 2024}}
He obtained his [[PhD]] at the Department of [[mathematics]] of [[King's College London]], England in September 1980.<ref name=Bio/>

In 1985 he briefly held a position as "Professore di ruolo" in Mathematics at "Liceo Scientifico Albert Einstein" in Turin.

He then joined the Space Systems Group of [[Aeritalia]] (later called [[Alenia Spazio]] S.p.A. and now Thales Alenia Space Italia S.p.A.) in Turin on 19 September 1985, and immediately got involved in the design of new space missions.<ref name=Bio/>

In 2002 he was awarded the "[[Giordano Bruno]] Award" by the SETI League, "for his efforts to establish a radio observatory on the far side of the [[Moon]]."<ref name=SETIaward/>

After his early retirement from Alenia Spazio S.p.A. on 30 December 2004, he taught at Polytechnic University of Turin for five years (2005-2009) at Post-Doctoral level. He was Advisor to Ph.D. candidates in the Aerospace and Electronics Departments of Polytechnic University of Turin.

Since 2010 he was the Director for Scientific Space Exploration of the [[International Academy of Astronautics]] (IAA, based in Paris, France).<ref name=IAA>{{cite web|url=http://resources.iaaseti.org/paris14.pdf|title=Fifth_IAA_Search_for_Life_Signatures_Symposium|publisher=[[International Academy of Astronautics]]|date=March 2014}}</ref>

From 2012 to 2021, he served as Chair of the IAA [[SETI]] Permanent Committee.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://iaaseti.org | title=Overview}}</ref>

He had published 149 scientific and technical papers.{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}}

Maccone died of a heart attack on 20 August 2025, at the age of 77.<ref>[https://www.lastampa.it/torino/2025/08/20/news/e__morto_il_fisico_claudio_maccone_progetto_un_radiotelescopio_per_il_lato_nascosto_della_luna-15277409/ È morto il fisico Claudio Maccone: progettò un radiotelescopio per il lato nascosto della Luna] {{in lang|it}}</ref>

== Books ==
* 1994 ''[[Telecommunications]], [[Karhunen–Loève theorem|KLT]] and [[Theory of relativity|Relativity]]'', IPI Press, Colorado Springs, USA<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://unov.tind.io/record/67765|title=Telecommunications, KLT and relativity|first=Claudio|last=Maccone|series=Textbooks in Science and Mathematics |date=31 July 1994|publisher=IPI Press|isbn=978-1-880930-04-5 |via=Library Catalogue}}</ref>
* 1998 ''The Sun as a [[Gravitational lens|Gravitational Lens]]: Proposed Space Missions'', IPI Press, Colorado Springs, USA (proposing [[FOCAL (spacecraft)|FOCAL]] space telescope), IAA Book Award 1999
* 2009 ''Deep Space Flight and Communications – Exploiting the Sun as a Gravitational Lens'', Praxis-Springer<ref name=Bio/><ref>{{cite book|title=Deep Space Flight and Communications: Exploiting the Sun as a Gravitational Lens|author=Maccone, Claudio|year=2009|publisher=Praxis-Springer|isbn=978-3-540-72942-6|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=3-540-72942-9}}</ref> The book was translated into Chinese by 2014 and awarded the IAA Book Award in 2018<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQQchrFBizE|title=Claudio Maccone - Speech at IAA Dinner in Paris on March 26 2019|date=20 November 2020|via=YouTube}}</ref>
* 2012 ''Mathematical SETI - Statistics, Signal Processing, Space Missions''<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-27437-4|title=Mathematical SETI|first=Claudio|last=Maccone|date=31 July 2012|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-27437-4 |isbn=978-3-642-27436-7 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> 
* 2021 ''Evo-SETI – Life Evolution Statistics on Earth and Exoplanets''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-51931-5|title=Evo-SETI|first=Claudio|last=Maccone|date=31 July 2020|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-51931-5 |isbn=978-3-030-51930-8 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> It won the Mathematical Astrobiology, IAA Book Award 2022.
* 2024 ''The Living Galaxy'', co-authored with [[Eugenio Mieli]] and [[Andrea M. F. Valli]]

==Honours and awards==
* The central [[main-belt]] binary asteroid [[11264 Claudiomaccone]] was named in Maccone's honor<ref>{{cite web | title=JPL Small-Body Database Browser |url=https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?sstr=11264;orb=1}}</ref>
* Maccone was a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) and an Associate of “Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica (INAF)” in Italy.
* Since December 2021 Maccone was serving as Chair of the IAA Moon Farside Protection Permanent Committee. His Co-chair is Prof. Jack O. Burns ([[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado at Boulder]]).
* On 8 February 2024, Maccone gave his third speech at the United Nations COPUOS in Vienna about the Moon Farside Protection.
* On 21–22 March 2024, Maccone and co-workers run the First IAA Symposium on Moon Farside Protection in Turin<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.moonfarsideprotection.org/|title=Moon Farside Protection|website=Moon Farside Protection}}</ref>
